lines.en: What makes a pun work is not the joke itself, but the split second it takes the listener to catch it.
It is said that a pun is the lowest form of wit, usually by people who cannot make one.
Were the sign outside the restaurant to say 'we serve food here', it would be no less honest than most jokes.
However old a joke may be, it is new to anyone hearing it for the first time.
Not until you explain a joke do you realize how much of it lived in the timing.
The comedian's silence, perfectly placed, got a bigger laugh than any of his words.
What children laugh at without reason, adults laugh at with relief.
The translation of the joke, though word-perfect, landed in complete silence.
Little is shared across every culture on Earth except the sound of laughter.
Rarely does a meeting need less laughter, whatever the agenda claims.
What the audience forgives in a comedian is everything except being boring on purpose.
It is the unexpected word in an ordinary sentence that does the work of the whole joke.
Were humor to follow rules, the funniest people alive would be the ones who wrote the rulebook.
Not until you have bombed in front of a silent crowd do you understand why comedians fear nothing else.
However painful the moment, give it a year and it may return as your best story.
